comments.author: sandesh-sp
comments.body:
> Just to make sure I understand opt 2 correctly. For the September deliverable, we could show a minimal set of fields in the UI for deck.gl for example only the Core tab with name, URL and type. For everything else, users would edit the mission config json directly. Then we incrementally expose more tabs and fields as we validate what each one means in the deck.gl context. Does that sound right?

Yes, this is what I'm thinking. As we'll be the one to create these tools initially, we can use mission config json for the initial version. It is also tricky to add all the configs, specially for handling UI/layout config, in the current Mission Config page.

> Is that already in one of the branches / still in progress? I have not seen it in the codebase yet.

[feat/modern-layout](https://github.com/NASA-IMPACT/MMGIS/tree/feat/modern-layout) is the working branch for layout changes. This will probably be reviewed and merged into [epic/modern-ui](https://github.com/NASA-IMPACT/MMGIS/tree/epic/modern-ui) by early next week. This branch is where we'll merge all the layout and styling PRs until they're ready to be merged to development branch.

> I may be missing some context here but from what I've seen so far i'd be in favor of going that route since we could likely do it much better than extending the existing configure page.

Our own tool builder was a core part of the value proposition we outlined during the workshop last year. After we decided to fork MMGIS, we briefly discussed developing a custom tool builder on top of it, but that conversation was sidelined as we wanted get the basics working like you mentioned.

> It seems better to get the basics working first and revisit it afterwards

Yes, once we complete the September deliverable, we should have this discussion again. The outcome will likely shape how much effort we put into extending the current Mission Config page as well.
